verdict.summary: You register an OAuth app from your own Apollo settings, and Apollo has to approve the registration, but no further app review is needed before other Apollo users can connect; the Marketplace listing is optional and needs 3+ connected teams. The catches are that on many plans only Admins or Billing and Seat Managers can authorize third-party apps, and rate limits and enrichment credits are shared per customer team.

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: Apollo says you can test in the playground once registration is approved, but doesn't publish how long approval takes. The range is our estimate.

timeToProd.assumes: An agent that searches and reads contacts and writes records on behalf of users from any Apollo team, without a Marketplace listing; listing adds 3+ connected teams and a Partner review that answers within 5 business days.
timeToProd.waitingOn: Apollo approving the OAuth registration (no published SLA). No separate app review for non-listed use.

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: The docs mention only registration approval. That no other review is needed comes from Nango's guide, so we label the range inferred.

verdict.cost: No developer or Marketplace fee. Calls run under the customer's Apollo plan: rate limits depend on their plan, and enrichment endpoints consume their credits.

prerequisites.item: An Apollo account with access to Settings > Integrations > API
prerequisites.why: OAuth registration lives in your Apollo settings, under API Keys > OAuth registration.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: The docs don't state a plan requirement for registering.

prerequisites.item: HTTPS redirect URLs (up to 4), an app name, a logo, scopes and a description of your organization's purpose
prerequisites.why: These are the registration fields. Registration requires Apollo's approval.

prerequisites.item: End users with permission to authorize third-party apps
prerequisites.why: On plans with custom permission profiles, users need 'Can authorize third-party apps/integrations via OAuth'. On other plans, they need the Admin or Billing and Seat Manager profile.

scopeTiers.impact: Covers identity plus searching and reading people and contacts. It needs only the one-time registration approval. Each scope maps to specific public API endpoints.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: reviewRequired=true reflects the registration approval, which applies to all scopes.

scopeTiers.impact: Lets the agent create and update records as the authorizing user. Requests act as the user who granted the token, so Apollo permissions and ownership apply.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: Only opportunity_write appears verbatim. Other write scopes weren't listed on the page we read.

scopeTiers.impact: Optional. It gives visibility in Apollo's marketplace and referral commissions. The Partner team replies within 5 business days, then reviews your listing before publishing.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: The 1–3 week figure is our estimate. The 5 business days is Apollo's.

steps.title: Open the API integration settings
steps.detail: Sign in to Apollo and go to Settings > Integrations > API, then click OAuth registration.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: The console URL is our best guess at the SPA route. The docs give only the menu path.

steps.title: Draft the registration details
steps.detail: Write the app description and organization purpose, choose least-privilege scopes (for example read_user_profile, contacts_search, person_read), and list up to 4 HTTPS redirect URLs.

steps.title: Submit the registration and copy credentials
steps.detail: Enter the name, logo, redirect URLs and scopes, then submit. Copy the client secret immediately, because it's shown only when generated.

steps.title: Wait for registration approval
steps.detail: Apollo approves the registration before you can test it in the playground.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: Approval is sourced. No duration is published.

steps.title: Implement the authorization code flow
steps.detail: Redirect to https://app.apollo.io/#/oauth/authorize?client_id=...&redirect_uri=...&response_type=code&scope=...&state=... and exchange the code at POST https://app.apollo.io/api/v1/oauth/token.

steps.title: Handle the 30-day token and refresh
steps.detail: Access tokens expire after 30 days. Refreshing revokes the existing pair automatically, so store the new tokens atomically and avoid concurrent refreshes.

steps.title: Build rate-limit and credit handling
steps.detail: Limits are per team, in fixed windows per endpoint, with minute, hour and day caps. On 429, honour retry-after, or wait 60s for PLATFORM_RATE_LIMIT. Warn users that enrichment calls spend their credits.

steps.title: Explain the authorizing-user requirement
steps.detail: Add a pre-connect note telling users that an Apollo Admin, a Billing and Seat Manager, or a user with the OAuth-authorize permission must click Connect.

steps.title: Launch to customers
steps.detail: Enable the Connect Apollo button. No further Apollo review is documented for non-listed apps.

evidence.label: unverified
evidence.note: That review is only needed for Marketplace listing comes from Nango's guide.

steps.title: Apply for a Marketplace listing (optional)
steps.detail: Once 3+ separate Apollo teams use the integration via OAuth only, submit the partner application form. Apollo replies within 5 business days, then reviews your listing before publishing.

Implement the code flow, refresh and token storage
Build per-team rate-limit handling with retry-after

Copy the client secret when it's displayed

blockers.symptom: A customer's regular user can't complete the connection
blockers.cause: Only users with the 'Can authorize third-party apps/integrations via OAuth' permission, or the Admin or Billing and Seat Manager profile, can authorize.
blockers.fix: Ask an Apollo admin to connect, or to grant the permission on plans with custom profiles.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: The exact error shown to the user isn't documented.

blockers.symptom: Can't test in the playground right after registering
blockers.cause: The registration hasn't been approved yet.
blockers.fix: Wait for Apollo's approval, and contact Apollo support if it stalls.

blockers.cause: A PLATFORM_RATE_LIMIT response, rather than an endpoint quota.
blockers.fix: Wait the 60 seconds given in suggestions, then retry.

blockers.symptom: Agent hits rate limits quickly for a free-plan customer
blockers.cause: Free plans allow as little as 50 requests/min, 200/hour and 600/day, shared across the whole team.
blockers.fix: Batch, cache and spread work across windows, and check limits via the usage stats endpoint.

blockers.symptom: New scopes don't appear in existing tokens
blockers.cause: Editing scopes requires repeating the whole authorization flow.
blockers.fix: Prompt every connected user to reconnect after a scope change.

blockers.symptom: Endpoint returns unauthorized with an OAuth token but works with an API key
blockers.cause: OAuth supports only the endpoints in Apollo's public API docs, and some endpoints need a master API key.
blockers.fix: Stick to public endpoints with matching scopes. Master-key-only endpoints aren't available to OAuth apps.

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: Whether master-key endpoints are blocked for OAuth is our inference.

nuances.text: Access tokens last 30 days, which is unusually long. Refreshing revokes the existing tokens.
OAuth requests act as the user who granted the token, while API-key requests act differently. Data visibility follows that user's Apollo permissions.
Rate limits are per team, not per user or token, use fixed windows per endpoint, and child workspaces share the parent's limits. Your agent competes with the customer's other tools.
Enrichment endpoints consume the customer's credits, so an agent that enriches aggressively costs the customer money.
The Marketplace accepts integrations built on Apollo's MCP Server as well as the REST API, and pays listed partners 15–20% referral commission.
The authorize URL is a hash route in Apollo's web app (/#/oauth/authorize), so it always returns HTTP 200 and errors render client-side rather than as HTTP redirects.

evidence.label: tested
evidence.note: GET https://app.apollo.io/#/oauth/authorize?client_id=test returned 200 on 2026-10-20 (the fragment isn't sent to the server).
